text:
leo: rolled an adaptive early-exit + token-trim policy to a 8% canary (prod) at 09:07 UTC. quick brief: aim was to cut p50 and reduce wasted tokens for short-to-mid sequences without changing model weights. :rocket:
anita: high level change? config diff?
leo: two runtime hooks: (1) early_exit heuristic looks for stable logit temp over a sliding 6-token window and truncates generation when confidence threshold met; (2) dynamic trim removes up to 2 trailing padding tokens added by legacy prompt framing for requests < 64 tokens. both guarded by per-route opt-in.
carter: bench numbers please. also any eval impact on quality?
leo: ran 90m live-replay + adversarial prompt set. Results for mixed short/mid workloads: p50 down 11ms -> 4ms (~64% rel), p95 down 58ms -> 39ms (~33% rel). Token cost per 1M tokens reduced ~18% (mostly from early-exit on deterministic short replies and less padding).
qa-bot: automated evals: pass rate on our core-quality suite dropped 0.4 percentage points (97.3% -> 96.9%) on a tiny subset of completion-diverse prompts. flagged for manual review but not a widespread regression.
anita: can you paste the runtime flags so SRE and QE can reproduce?
leo: pasted snippet:```json
{
  "early_exit": {
    "enabled": true,
    "confidence_threshold": 0.92,
    "stability_window": 6
  },
  "token_trim": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_trim_tokens": 2,
    "apply_if_input_len_lt": 64
  },
  "routes": ["/chat/short","/reply/quick"]
}```
carter: any tail regressions for long-run inference (>=1024 tokens)?
leo: no meaningful impact on >1024 token runs in the canary telemetry. We did observe one AZ with transient p99 bump tied to a GC spike on an older runtime container; not related to the early-exit logic. ops patched the node.
perf-bot: perf-run id perf_2026_05_11_0907 - dashboard https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/canary/1798765432 - traces + cost breakdown uploaded. :white_check_mark:
anita: rollout plan?
leo: propose 8% -> 25% (45m) -> 60% (90m) -> 100% with a hard p99 quality gate: if core-quality drop >0.5pp or p99 latency regresses >10% revert immediately. I'll create the rollout ticket with rollback playbook.
carter: add a canary probe that injects deterministic replies to ensure early-exit doesn't cut needed tokens. also add the QA failing examples into a watchlist for manual inspection.
leo: good call. scheduling ops window at 22:00 UTC, @carter @anita ok?
anita: fine. carter: yep.
leo: TL;DR: adaptive early-exit + token-trim gives big p50 wins (~64%) and ~18% token cost reduction; tiny dip in one quality subset (0.4pp) under investigation; staged rollout planned tonight with strict quality gate. Will post the final perf artifacts and QA notes after rollout. :tada:
